summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and chest pain after being found crawling on the ground due to respiratory distress. He had recently left two prior hospitals against medical advice. Evaluation revealed multifocal pneumonia and acute exacerbation of COPD, with evidence of acute on chronic systolic heart failure and mild acute kidney injury. He was treated with levofloxacin, steroids, bronchodilators, and diuresis. An echocardiogram confirmed severe left ventricular dysfunction. He had a brief asymptomatic run of ventricular tachycardia. Despite efforts to arrange methadone treatment, no immediate placement was available. The patient understood the risks but chose to leave against medical advice to attend a future methadone clinic appointment, expressing a desire to become sober. He was discharged on antibiotics, heart failure medications, and supportive prescriptions with close follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
